messages:
sam: deploy-bot just flagged canary p95 latency at 2.7s (threshold 2.5s). auto-rollback did NOT trigger due to traffic-slice exception. anyone on call can take a look?

deploy-bot: ALERT @channel: Canary latency breach detected. p95=2.7s (>2.5s). error-rate +0.9pp. Auto-rollback skipped: rule "traffic-slice-exempt" matched. Recommended actions: 1) Pin canary traffic to v3.1.3 for dedicated pools, 2) Consider manual rollback to v3.1.4 for canary. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/release-rollback 
Suggested CLI: `redwoodctl releases rollback --env canary --to v3.1.4 --reason "latency-spike"`

anya: ack. I'm release lead for this window — do we have evidence of correctness regressions or is this infra? metrics show increased token generation time and some 5xxs on the kv-cache endpoints.

lee: i'm oncall. seeing KV miss rate spike at the same time as latency. suspect kvcache invalidation after the new kernel flags. i'm going to hold the rollout and execute a targeted rollback for the canary slice only.

lee: running: `redwoodctl releases rollback --slice canary --to v3.1.4 --no-wait`
```
Rolling back canary slice -> v3.1.4
Drain connections to new instances
Applying version pin for canary routing
```

ria: should we also pin Dedicated pools for customers with reserved capacity? some customers are experiencing higher latency and we promised stability. if we pin, we'll need a customer-facing note.

sam: +1 to pin dedicated pools. workflow: 1) pin model-version in routing-config for affected pools, 2) create a small release-note update and send to CS for immediate outreach. I can open the PR for the routing-config patch: https://git.redwood/releases/patches/PR-4832

deploy-bot: NOTE: For Dedicated pools use `redwoodctl pools set-version --pool dedicated-eu-west --version v3.1.3`. If pin is applied, automatic rollouts will skip v3.1.5.

lee: pinned dedicated-eu-west to v3.1.3. command output: `OK -> pool updated (dedicated-eu-west)`.

sre-oncall: warning — v3.1.4 -> v3.1.3 rollback is safe for model artifacts, but there is a kv-cache schema change in 3.1.5 only. confirm no migrations were applied. if migration flag was flipped, do NOT roll back without cache flush. Runbook snippet: https://redwood/runbooks/kvcache-flush

anya: good catch. lee, can you confirm whether the migration flag `--kv-schema=v2` was enabled in the canary?

lee: checked — flag was enabled on 3.1.5 instances only. canary we rolled back from was 3.1.5, migration flag was toggled, but we reverted the flag during rollout. i've scheduled a KV flush job to be safe: `jobs/flush-kv-cache --target canary --quiet`.

ria: CS heads, pls be ready: i'll draft a one-paragraph customer note describing the stability hit and the rollback. include: what happened, action taken (partial rollback + pin), impact (brief downtime risk: none), next steps (monitoring + followup when we promote 3.1.5).

cs-team: on it. will send targeted messages to the 4 affected Dedicated customers in eu-west within 15 minutes. template ready: "We're temporarily pinning your pool to v3.1.3 after a latency spike; no action required on your side."

sam: logging comms in release-tracker: https://git.redwood/releases/tracker/issue-721. Also adding a note to release notes: "Hotfix: rolling back canary from 3.1.5 due to KV cache latency spike; v3.1.5 will remain blocked until further testing."

lee: rollback completed for canary slice. p95 back to 1.9s within 3 minutes. :thumbsup:

anya: closing the canary window early. leave the dedicated pin in place until we validate a hotfix. will schedule a postmortem if customer impact exceeds 1hr.

deploy-bot: RESOLVED: Canary alert closed automatically after rollback. Telemetry link: https://telemetry/redwood/canary/3337772222

sam: thanks team. leaving a checklist for follow-ups: 1) SRE validate kv-cache flush, 2) QA to run perf regression on 3.1.5, 3) PM to update release notes and customer comms, 4) decide lift-pin window in next 24h.

sre-oncall: running kvcache validation job now, will report in #eng-sre.

anya: thread archived once SRE confirms. great coordination. :rocket:
